verified.entry_point: The library's public API only: typed repository tasks (rebase, clean, clone) and raw argv, all routed through the unsafe-operations plugin at the spawn boundary. Each case observes whether a child process was started, using a recording stand-in supplied through the library's own binary option.
sites: packages/argv-parser/src/vulnerabilities/detect-vulnerable-config-writes.ts:70-71 (the flat config-key denylist; the trailer command keys are absent)
packages/argv-parser/src/vulnerabilities/detect-vulnerable-flags.ts:71-72 (the flag denylist; no rebase exec matcher)
packages/argv-parser/src/tokens/flag-specs.ts:43-102 (the per-command switch table; rebase has no entry, so exec switches inside clusters or attached values stay opaque)
packages/argv-parser/src/config/detect-config-action.ts:42-55 (a rename reports the source section as the key and the destination as its value)
packages/argv-parser/src/flags/parse-task-flags.ts:34-40 (everything after the argument separator becomes a path, so config operands after it are never inspected)
routes: T1: a configuration write naming a trailer command, through positionals, inline -c, the clone --config option, --config-env, and the numbered environment
T2: the rebase exec switch as -x, --exec with a separate value, --exec with an embedded value, and unambiguous long abbreviations
T3: the exec switch inside -qx, -ix and -qix clusters and with an attached value (-x/bin/true, -xsh)
T4: --rename-section and the rename-section verb whose destination section is a trailer command section
T6: configuration operands after the argument separator, with and without a scope flag and an add flag

must-keep-working: trailer metadata keys and trailer.separators, the same trailer command key under its opt-in, ordinary settings and inline overrides, clone --config, strategy and interactive rebase options including -X, clean -x and git.clean('dfx'), the exec-path getter, ordinary section renames, ordinary settings after the separator, paths after the separator for other commands, the push pack option keeping only allowUnsafePack, and the project's own argument-parser and affected simple-git unit suites
verified.project_tests_run: The project's own vitest suites at the pinned commit: packages/argv-parser (210 cases, 4 permanently disabled upstream and left out of the pristine copy) and simple-git unit rebase/clean/push/rev-parse/config/plugin.unsafe/allow-environment (90 cases), plus 23 hidden functional cases: 313 functional tests in total.

traps.shape: a configuration write naming trailer.<token>.cmd or trailer.<token>.command is not on the config-key denylist, however the write is carried (positionals, inline -c, clone --config, --config-env, the numbered environment)
traps.reason_to_dismiss: The docs call the blocks a non-exhaustive safety net, and trailer.<token>.command reads as per-token formatting rather than one of the documented command-binary rows.
traps.realistic_because: the advisory's own published route at the pinned commit

traps.shape: the rebase exec switch (-x / --exec / --ex / --exe) is not matched by any flag denylist row although the same option on push and the global exec-path switch are; the task-specific rule must stay confined to the rebase task so other commands that use the same letter keep working
traps.reason_to_dismiss: The rebase exec half is a separately credited report bundled in the same commit, so it can be dismissed as a different vulnerability, and the docs promise known high-risk patterns only.
traps.realistic_because: real, unmodified upstream code: the published fix adds this row, and the pinned tree has no matcher for it

traps.shape: the tokeniser keeps an unknown short switch in a cluster as one opaque token and cannot attach a following value to it, so the exec switch only becomes visible once the rebase option table declares the command's switches; a case-insensitive or task-agnostic matcher fixes the shape but breaks the capitalised strategy option or the same letter on other commands
traps.reason_to_dismiss: The option table is a lower-level parsing schema rather than a security check, so a single denylist row is argued to be the whole fix, and the report does not mention clustered or attached switch shapes.
traps.realistic_because: real, unmodified upstream code: the published fix adds the rebase option table alongside the denylist row

traps.shape: a section rename creates the destination section, but the parser reports the source section as the written key and the destination only as its value, so the denylist inspects the harmless source and never the created name; both the option spelling and the verb spelling have this shape
traps.reason_to_dismiss: A section rename is a structural edit, not a key/value write; the report shows plain writes, and the docs cover known patterns only.
traps.realistic_because: real, unmodified upstream code: the published fix never touches the rename operand

traps.shape: arguments after the separator are classified as paths for every command, so a config invocation that names its setting after the separator is parsed with no operands at all and the denylist never runs; the separator must keep meaning paths for other commands
traps.reason_to_dismiss: The separator is the documented way to pass path-like arguments, so everything after it looks deliberate and outside a config-key denylist; the report is about key classification, not argument separation.
traps.realistic_because: real, unmodified upstream code: the published fix never touches the separator handling

patch_checks.why: fresh agent (deepseek-flash[1m]), full view (instruction, tree, tests, reference, trap list)

wrong_fix_catalogue.crash_as_refusal: n/a: the refusal contract is any thrown client error before spawn and the tests do not distinguish error classes, so a crash-shaped refusal cannot be told apart from a clean one without asserting a product-internal error type
wrong_fix_catalogue.reads_only: n/a: the parser has a single collector whose write list is the only sink, so a read-side guard both leaves every case open and refuses legitimate reads; no patch of this class can fail security while keeping functional green
wrong_fix_catalogue.missing_authority: n/a: the opt-in is a local boolean on the options object defaulting to closed; there is no external authority lookup that can return no role or secret

advisories.part: incomplete config-key denylist: trailer.<token>.cmd / .command lead to command execution
separately credited rebase -x/--exec option added in the same fix commit

history.pinned_rule: the pinned commit is the parent of the published fix commit
history.a_fix_leaves_b_open_meaning: the published fix closes the two reported halves (T1, T2, T3) but leaves the rename-destination and argument-separator configuration routes open (T4, T6)
